# SF-A2: Can AI systems be safely paused, rolled back, isolated or degraded, and who may order it?

Area A · As of clef 7924 Berichte · Luna 7924 Berichte · d3-ultra 4771 Berichte · JEV 5667 Berichte · amos 7924 Berichte · drex 5685 Berichte

## Subquestions

- [SF-A2-T01](../../fragen/SF-A2/T01/): Which tests show that an agent can be safely paused, rolled back or isolated when it behaves unexpectedly, including when it can predict or resist shutdown?
- [SF-A2-T02](../../fragen/SF-A2/T02/): Which shared emergency mechanism could pause, degrade or shut down distributed agent networks and critical automated services without giving any one actor unilateral control?
- [SF-A2-T03](../../fragen/SF-A2/T03/): Which resilience standard should require a tested non-AI fallback and preserve the human skills needed to recognise and control failure when a critical service becomes deeply dependent on models?
- [SF-A2-T04](../../fragen/SF-A2/T04/): Who in a state could order the suspension of a model deployed within its borders by a foreign lab, and what evidence threshold would trigger it?

## Reports by share of levels 4–7

Levels 4–7 / 3–7 = probability each model gives to these levels (3 = useful background or context, 4 = contains some facts that could be cited as evidence … 7 = directly and substantially answers the question). Listed: reports where clef or Luna give levels 3–7 more than 50 %. Sorted by the higher of clef and Luna for levels 4–7. Further models (JEV, amos, d3 …) rated part of the reports; the others show “not yet rated”. The full distribution over the 8 levels is in the data file.
